top5.why: Core execution path; matches audited Safe 1.3.0 with no deviation found.
Signature and contract-signature handling is the main attack surface but is the standard audited logic.
Modules bypass signatures, so an enabled malicious module would drain funds, but enabling needs owner approval.
Proxy init via arbitrary initializer is the typical front-run target, but the salt binds the initializer.
Forwards unknown calls to the handler with appended sender, which is safe only if the handler is trusted.
Gov or sub-gov can make arbitrary calls from the farming contract, a trust and centralization risk rather than an external exploit.
Relies on a 1-2h TWAP with 0.5% bounds, and update_twap is callable by anyone.
Anyone can reset the TWAP snapshot; the window logic may be griefed or timed.
External incentivizer contracts are summed into vote counts, so a malicious one added via the timelock would inflate voting power.
While admin_initialized is false the admin executes without queueing, bypassing the delay.
Admin-gated upgrade with delegatecall to an arbitrary implementation; gating looks correct.
Delegatecalls init data to the new implementation before the admin is set in the constructor.
Admin transfer is onlyProxyAdmin and has no zero-address check.
Uses EIP-1967 slots, so collision risk is low, but implementation selectors can be shadowed by the proxy's own functions.
Proxy-level function shadows the implementation's; low severity.
Share price comes from pool slot0 spot price with no TWAP or deviation check, so a flash-loan price push lets a one-sided depositor mint inflated shares and extract value on withdraw.
Valuation uses spot-derived amounts, so it moves with sandwiched price.
Shares are burned after the external transfers, and it has no reentrancy guard or slippage minimum.
The owner-chosen swap has no price limit or slippage bound and the fee recipient is arbitrary, so it is sandwichable and a trust risk.
Proportional rounding and the first-share and donation edge case.
Complex restore, re-add and buy-back accounting where an error could cause insolvency; no concrete exploit found.
Segment linked-list rewrites can desync from real pool positions.
Rounding between cost, tax, held and settle amounts relies on a 1000 wei allowance.
Partial-fill tick math with rounding-up spend loops.
ETH is sent to the owner after close; it is nonReentrant and followed by a solvency check.
Calls a user-supplied callback after creation; the result is not trusted state.
The initializer runs in the same transaction, so there is no front-run window.
CREATE2 salt is bound to the initializer and nonce.
Singleton lives in slot 0, which matches the Safe layout.
Uses a revert to return the address; no state is persisted.
NFT mint and burn bookkeeping on ERC20 floor changes can desync for whitelisted or fractional balances, but no theft path found.
Values up to 50 are treated as NFT ids, so small ERC20 amounts are ambiguous.
Pops from the owned list and underflows if an address has more ERC20 units than NFTs.
The LayerZero credit mint path depends on the per-chain 721 cap and bank state, so it can revert and block inbound transfers.
Canonical Uniswap v3 pool, identical across the variants; no deviation found.
Anyone can call it with a chosen solver and users and it makes an external callback, but each user is paid their own signed price.
No validation of price, balance or approval; users can set a bad price, which is documented.
Rounds down against the user, with dust-level loss.
View only; repeated users are not accounted for.
View only helper.
When nothing is claimable, lastETHBalance is not updated but totalRewards is increased, so repeated calls (even with an empty array) inflate totalRewards and let a holder drain the contract's ETH.
View logic ignores its local totalRewards_, so reported values are wrong.
Never sets receivedAirdrop and mints new tokens that share past rewards, so the per-token accounting is diluted.
The fee goes to an owner-set destination; the transfer lock is owner-controlled.
Transfers are locked unless unlocked or sent by the owner.
